# Issue #34: cache throws away the hot key

We use `LRUCache(2)` for session lookups. After `put("a", 1)`, `put("b", 2)`,
`get("a")`, `put("c", 3)` I expected `"b"` to be dropped, since `"a"` was just read.
Instead `"a"` disappears and `"b"` stays. Reads do not seem to count as use.
The code is in `lru/cache.py`.

tests/test_cache.py

   6| 
   7|     Both get() (on a hit) and put() count as a use of the key. When a new key

   9|     Updating the value of an existing key never evicts anything.

The fix is complete. The bug was in `get()`: on a hit it returned the value but never re-inserted the key, so the key's position in the insertion-order dict (which encodes recency) was never updated. Now a hit re-inserts the key, moving it to most-recently-used, matching the documented behavior.

Verified:
- The exact issue scenario (`put a`, `put b`, `get a`, `put c`) now evicts `"b"` and keeps `"a"` ✓
- All 3 existing tests pass ✓
- Edge cases: misses leave cache unchanged, updates don't evict, capacity-1 works, `__contains__` doesn't count as a use ✓

arguments.summary: Fixed LRUCache.get() in lru/cache.py: on a hit it now re-inserts the key (del + re-add) so the key moves to most-recently-used, matching the documented behavior that reads count as a use. Previously get() returned the value without updating recency, so a recently-read key could be evicted while a stale key survived (the issue's scenario: after put a, put b, get a, put c, "a" was wrongly evicted). Verified the issue scenario now evicts "b" and keeps "a", all existing tests pass, and edge cases (misses, updates, capacity 1, __contains__) behave correctly.
